  Exam Date & Time: 20-Jun-2024 (02:30 PM - 05:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MIT BLR - BTech VI Semester - End Semester Makeup Examination - June -2024  
  Big Data Analytics [CSE-3272]  
  Marks: 50                                                                             Duration: 180 mins.  
  PART-A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1)           A retail company wants to analyze customer purchase history using MapReduce. The  
  data includes customer IDs, product IDs, and purchase quantities. Demonstrate a  
  (5)  
  MapReduce job to calculate the total revenue generated for each product category.  
  A)  
  B)      Interpret the output operations in DStream with a suitable example.                         (3)  
  C)      Relate and explain the two different ways of loading data into RDDs with syntax.            (2)  
  2)           You are tasked with building a music recommendation system using Spark ALS.  
  Analyse and illustrate the steps involved from data preparation to evaluating the model's  
  (5)  
  performance, with code snippets.  
  A)  
  B)      Demonstrate different ways to create RDDs programmatically in Spark with appropriate  
  syntax and examples                                                                  (3)  
  
  C)      Use two examples of ROC curves, one representing a well-performing model and  
  another for a poorly performing model. Discuss the visual cues that indicate each           (2)  
  scenario.  
  
  3)           Predict the steps involved in the construction and evaluation of K-means clustering that  
  can be employed to uncover distinct customer groups based on their purchase behavior  
  and preferences and explain Spark's capabilities for handling large-scale e-commerce        (5)  
  A)      data.  
  
  B)      Interpret the benefits and challenges of using Spark for data analysis and machine  
  learning tasks.                                                                             (3)  
  
  C)      Analyse and explain how can you handle the trade-off between network size and  
  computational efficiency while using GraphX for large networks.                             (2)  
  
  4)           Imagine you have a large corpus of text data, like news articles or social media posts. (5)  
  You're interested in understanding the relationships between entities mentioned in this  
  data. This could be words, phrases, or even topics. Leveraging GraphX, design a  
  A)      framework to construct a co-occurrence network from this textual data. Here's what you  
  need to consider:  
  Perdict how will you clean and tokenize the text data to extract relevant entities?
